headline: Resistance opposes motion—friction, drag, and obstacles slow everything that moves
universal_truth: Resistance is inevitable; the question is not if you'll face it, but how you'll handle it
fun_facts: Without friction, you couldn't walk—your feet would slip like on ice
Sharks have skin that reduces drag so efficiently, scientists study it to design better swimsuits
The space station requires periodic boosts because even in space, tiny atmospheric drag slows it down
discussion_questions: What's creating friction in your life right now?
When is resistance helpful versus harmful?
How do you reduce friction for your goals?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every moving thing encounters resistance. Friction slows your car. Air drag limits your speed. Obstacles block your path. Resistance is universal—understanding it helps you work with it, around it, or through it.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often see resistance as purely negative—something to eliminate. But resistance plays important roles. How should we think about it?

options.text: Resistance is neutral—sometimes it's necessary (friction lets you walk) and sometimes it's harmful (drag slows you); the goal is appropriate resistance, not zero resistance
options.response: Yes. Without friction, cars couldn't brake. Without some resistance, there's no traction. The goal is managing resistance—reducing it where harmful, maintaining it where helpful.

options.text: Resistance should be minimized whenever possible
options.response: Often true, but not always—some resistance is necessary for control...

q1.title: Types of Resistance
q1.script: Friction between surfaces. Drag through fluids. Inertia resisting change. Obstacles in paths. Resistance takes many forms, but all oppose motion. Identifying the type helps you address it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Types of Resistance"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Reducing Friction
q2.script: Lubricants reduce friction. Streamlining reduces drag. Removing obstacles clears paths. You can't eliminate resistance, but you can minimize it where it hurts. Systems thinking asks: where's the friction?
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Productive Friction
q3.script: Some friction is valuable. Difficulty in learning creates deeper memory. Effort in exercise builds strength. Not all resistance is bad—some is necessary for growth. Easy isn't always better.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Resistance is inevitable. The question isn't if you'll face it, but how you'll handle it—reduce what's harmful, keep what's helpful.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 225. Tomorrow, we'll explore why things float—buoyancy. Until then, identify one source of friction you can reduce.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Friction Reduction - Smooth the Path
growTrack.activity: Pick a goal or habit you're pursuing. Where's the friction? What makes it harder than it needs to be? Can you reduce that friction—make it easier, remove an obstacle, create a smoother path? Less friction means more motion.
